office_does: A Grays Harbor County District Court judge, elected countywide, hears misdemeanors and gross misdemeanors, traffic infractions, protection orders, small claims and other limited civil cases, and sets bail.
race_blurb: Incumbent Megan Valentine, appointed in 2021 and the court's presiding judge for three and a half years, faces former District and Superior Court judge David Mistachkin, who lost his Superior Court seat in 2024. The race centers on the court's operations: Valentine runs on the programs she started, and Mistachkin on restoring staff morale and relations with the clerk, commissioners and other justice partners. No bar rating was found for either.

candidates.summary: Grays Harbor District Court judge since her 2021 appointment, elected in 2022, and presiding judge for three and a half years; previously a prosecutor, private attorney and foster-youth advocate.
highlights: Founded the DUI Therapeutic Court, which pairs treatment with intensive supervision [S1][S5]
Added pretrial monitoring to District Court probation services [S1]
Led the court's 2025 Blake refund effort covering about 2,500 eligible cases [S6][S7]
Presided over the court during its 2025 disputes with the county clerk over jury administration and with the commissioners over staffing [S8][S10]
Says a judge should not substitute their judgment for that of the elected prosecutor or jurors [S3]

experience.basis: Sitting judge since 2021 and presiding judge for three and a half years, running on her record of court programs and administration.

safety.basis: Prosecutor background and accountability framing, alongside founding a treatment-based DUI court and adding pretrial monitoring; she presents both as accountability plus treatment.

candidates.summary: Former Grays Harbor District Court judge (2015-2016) and Superior Court judge (2018 until his 2024 defeat); before that a criminal defense and family law attorney and partner at an Aberdeen firm.
highlights: District Court judge 2015-2016 by appointment; Superior Court judge from 2018 until losing re-election in 2024 [S1][S6][S8]
About 15 years in private practice, mostly criminal defense and family law [S3][S4]
Top priorities: public confidence in the court, staff morale, and relationships with justice partners and the commissioners [S3]
As a judge in 2016, described using deferred prosecution and sentences aimed at underlying issues to reduce reoffending [S4]

experience.basis: About eight years of prior judicial service plus commissioner and pro tem work, but he is the challenger, has been off the bench since his 2024 defeat, and pitches a change in how the court is run.

safety.basis: Formation mostly in criminal defense; as a District Court judge he described using deferred prosecution and sentences that address underlying issues to prevent reoffending.
